# The environment agents work in

::: {.callout-note}
Draft brief, tier C: skeleton. Bullets and references compiled from source discussions 01–08 (2026-11-16). `[LAB n]`, `[RESEARCH]`, `[PLAN]` and `[VERIFY]` mark what is still open. `vault:` paths point into the Obsidian vault.
:::

**Outcome (draft, #3):** give agents a versioned, reproducible environment, so tools, credentials and CI behave the same at run time as in testing. Check: the environment is built from a pinned definition, and a drift check fails loudly.

## Bullets available now
- Opener: what the OpenAI guide leaves out that costs a first-fleet reader most is "environment reproducibility -- no gotchas at run time". Its agent is a model, tools and instructions, with no runtime under it (04).
- Pin prompts, tools and configs by content hash and commit ID, with staged rollout and auto-rollback (OWASP ASI04, 07).
- Pinning the workflow isn't pinning what it calls: images, config and fetched skills need their own pins (02).
- Fail closed, don't degrade: GitHub's setup skips failed steps and works with whatever state it has (08).
- Own the runtime: a vendor default moved on 2026-10-28, and the repo-owned setup and 28-day retention stopped applying (08).
- Trade-off: `--bare` makes a run reproducible by dropping hooks and context files, so the reproducible mode loses the enforced rules (03).
- "all code should assume something will break, or take too long to respond" (01).
- The Clinejection chain links that live here: an arbitrary npm install and a shared cache (07).
- Build vs buy, and prefer open source (05).
